The last stop covers the helpers around the analysis: dependencies, git safety, AI
assistant files, notebook stubs, your global settings, and the Quarto configuration.
Calls that would change your machine, your global settings, or the outer git repository
are behind `RUN_*` flags set to `False`.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import shutil
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import framework as fw

root = fw.scaffold()
sandbox = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
```

## Packages

`packages_list()` reads the dependencies from `pyproject.toml` and the installed
versions from this environment.

```{python}
fw.packages_list()
```

`packages_status()` checks that `uv.lock` is current and the environment matches it.
Look for `missing`, the dependencies that are not installed.

```{python}
fw.packages_status()
```

The rest call `uv` and change `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, or the environment:
`package_add()` (`uv add`), `packages_install()` (`uv sync`), `packages_snapshot()`
(`uv lock`), `packages_restore()` (`uv sync --frozen`), and `packages_update()`
(`uv lock --upgrade`). Set the flag to add seaborn and see it appear in the list.

```{python}
RUN_PACKAGES = False

if RUN_PACKAGES:
    fw.package_add("seaborn")
    print(fw.packages_list())
```

## Git hooks

Framework can install a pre-commit hook that checks for private data, unignored
sensitive folders, and notebooks committed with outputs. `git_hooks_list()` shows the
checks; all are off in a new project.

```{python}
fw.git_hooks_list()
```

Whether the hook is installed is in `attrs`.

```{python}
fw.git_hooks_list().attrs
```

This project has no `.git` of its own; it sits inside the outer
`framework-test-projects` repository. Git would run the outer repository's hooks, so
`git_hooks_install()` refuses with an explanation. This error is expected here.

```{python}
try:
    fw.git_hooks_install()
except fw.FrameworkError as error:
    print(error)
```

`git_hooks_enable()` refuses the same way and leaves the settings unchanged: the check
stays off.

```{python}
try:
    fw.git_hooks_enable("check_notebook_outputs")
except fw.FrameworkError as error:
    print(str(error).splitlines()[0][:90], "...")
fw.git_hooks_list()[["hook", "enabled"]]
```

## Security audit

`git_security_audit()` checks that private folders and secrets are ignored, that git
does not track data in private folders, and (optionally) the history. It only reads,
unless `auto_fix=True`. Look at the summary lines. `local.sqlite` and the `published/`
bundles sit outside the data folders, but `.gitignore` excludes them, so they are not
reported as orphaned files.

```{python}
result = fw.git_security_audit(history_depth="shallow")
result.passed
```

## AI assistant files

New projects get an `AGENTS.md` (with `CLAUDE.md` pointing at it) and Framework skills
for the chosen assistants.

```{python}
print((root / "AGENTS.md").read_text()[:600])
sorted(p.name for p in (root / ".claude/skills").iterdir())
```

`ai_skills_update()` refreshes Framework's skills to the installed version. It keeps
skills you edited. An empty list means they were already current.

```{python}
fw.ai_skills_update(root)
```

## Notebooks, scripts, and stubs

`make_notebook()` creates a notebook from a stub. Without a type, the project's
`scaffold.notebook_format` decides; here it is `quarto`. These go into a temporary
folder so the project stays clean.

```{python}
print(fw.settings("scaffold.notebook_format"))
qmd = fw.make_notebook("Lab Values", dir=sandbox)
print(qmd.read_text()[:400])
```

An extension or `type=` picks another format, and `make_script()`, `make_qmd()`, and
`make_revealjs()` are the specific forms.

```{python}
made = [
    fw.make_notebook("lab-values.ipynb", dir=sandbox),
    fw.make_notebook("Quick Look", dir=sandbox, stub="minimal"),
    fw.make_script("Refresh Extract", dir=sandbox),
    fw.make_qmd("Survey Notes", dir=sandbox),
    fw.make_revealjs("Lab Meeting", dir=sandbox),
]
[p.name for p in made]
```

`stubs_list()` shows the stubs and where each comes from: the project's `stubs/`
folder, your personal templates, or Framework.

```{python}
fw.stubs_list()
```

`stubs_publish()` copies Framework's stubs into the project's `stubs/` folder to
customize. A project stub then wins over Framework's. This copies one, edits it, uses
it, and removes the folder again.

```{python}
copied = fw.stubs_publish("notebooks", stubs=["minimal"])
print([p.name for p in copied])

stub = fw.stubs_path("user") / "notebook-minimal.qmd"
stub.write_text(stub.read_text() + "\n## Study notes\n\nCohort: fictional BP study.\n")
print(fw.stubs_list(type="quarto"))
print(fw.make_notebook("with-project-stub", dir=sandbox, stub="minimal").read_text())

shutil.rmtree(fw.stubs_path("user"))
```

Personal templates live in your config folder and apply to every project.
`read_framework_template()` shows the one in use. Writing or resetting one changes your
global setup, so it is behind a flag.

```{python}
print(fw.framework_template_path("notebook"))
print(fw.read_framework_template("script"))
```

```{python}
RUN_TEMPLATES = False

if RUN_TEMPLATES:
    text = fw.read_framework_template("notebook")
    fw.write_framework_template("notebook", text.replace("Your Name", "Erik"))
    print(fw.read_framework_template("notebook")[:200])
    fw.reset_framework_template("notebook")
```

## Global settings and the project registry

Framework's global folder holds your defaults, the project registry, and templates.

```{python}
print(fw.config_dir())
fw.global_settings().keys()
```

`configure_global()` without arguments returns the global settings unchanged; with a
mapping it merges values in.

```{python}
current = fw.configure_global()
current.get("author", "(no author set)")
```

`project_list()` is the registry that `new()` adds to. The `exists` column marks
projects whose folder is gone; remove those with `project_unregister(id)`.

```{python}
fw.project_list()[["id", "path", "exists"]]
```

`config_sync()` copies settings and saved logins from the R package's config folder.
`dry_run=True` only reports.

```{python}
fw.config_sync(dry_run=True)
```

`load_settings_catalog()` is Framework's package defaults, with your
`settings-catalog.yml` merged over them. Look at the project types.

```{python}
catalog = fw.load_settings_catalog()
list(catalog["project_types"])
```

These change the registry or your defaults, so they are behind a flag.

```{python}
RUN_GLOBAL = False

if RUN_GLOBAL:
    pid = fw.project_register(sandbox)
    print(fw.project_list())
    fw.project_unregister(pid)
    fw.configure_global({"author": {"name": "Your Name"}})
```

## Quarto configuration

`_quarto.yml` was generated from the settings. `quarto_generate_all()` writes it from
explicit values; here it targets a copy so you can compare. Look at `output-dir`.

```{python}
copy = sandbox / "quarto-copy"
copy.mkdir()
written = fw.quarto_generate_all(
    copy, "project",
    render_dirs=fw.settings("render_dirs"),
    quarto_settings={"html": {"toc": False}},
    directories=fw.settings("directories"),
)
print([p.name for p in written])
print(written[0].read_text())
```

`quarto_regenerate()` rewrites the project's own files from its settings, after backing
them up under `.quarto_backups/`. It overwrites your edits, so it runs on a copy of the
project here.

```{python}
project_copy = sandbox / "py-project-copy"
shutil.copytree(root, project_copy, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
    ".venv", "inputs", "outputs", "published", "*.sqlite", "framework.db"))
regenerated = fw.quarto_regenerate(project_copy)
regenerated
```

```{python}
shutil.rmtree(sandbox)
```
